Update a roxygen2 file's row count for new observations

Source: R/update.R
sd_update_row_count.Rd

Companion to sd_update_roxygen(), but for new ROWS (respondents) instead of new variables. When a dataset gains observations but no new variables, the \describe{} block itself needs no change – only the row count recorded in the @format line (e.g. "... with 200 rows and 17 variables:") is now wrong. sd_update_row_count() corrects that number deterministically – no language model call is needed, because unlike a variable description, a row count has exactly one correct value.

Usage

sd_update_row_count(x, object_name, file = NULL, dry_run = TRUE)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object containing the CURRENT, full data (including the new rows).

object_name

Name the documented object has, e.g. "survey_data" – the same name used with sd_generate_roxygen().

file

Path to the existing roxygen2 file to update. Defaults to file.path("R", paste0(object_name, ".R")).

dry_run

If TRUE (the default), the updated text is only returned, not written to disk. Set to FALSE to write it to file (a .bak backup of the previous version is made first, as in sd_update_roxygen()).

Value

An object of class sd_row_count_update with elements text (the full updated file content), old_count, new_count, file, backup_file (path to the .bak copy, or NULL when dry_run = TRUE or nothing changed), and created.

Details

This function intentionally does NOT touch sd_document()'s descriptive text – its prose (respondent counts, distributions, and so on) is generated from the whole dataset and cannot be patched incrementally the way new variable descriptions can. Re-run sd_document() by hand if the row-count change is significant enough to warrant it. See sd_check_row_count() for a quick check of whether an update is needed at all.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# aineistoon on lisätty uusia vastaajia, muuttujat pysyivät samoina:
tulos <- sd_update_row_count(aineisto, "survey_data")
print(tulos)   # tarkista muutos ennen tallennusta
sd_update_row_count(aineisto, "survey_data", dry_run = FALSE)
} # }
